faq.q: How many implants does All-on-4 use?
faq.a: All-on-4 uses four titanium implants to support a whole arch of replacement teeth. faq.q: Can I leave the clinic with new teeth on the same day?

faq.q: Who is a good candidate for All-on-4 dental implants?
faq.a: All-on-4 suits people who have lost all the teeth in a jaw, are unhappy with their dentures, or have chewing and speech problems caused by tooth loss. h2_changes.old: What is B1 tooth shade? B1: A standout shade

faq.q: What is B1 tooth shade?
faq.a: B1 is a light shade in the B group of the VITA shade guide, the group with reddish-yellow hues. It is one of the most popular shades for veneers, crowns and whitening because it looks bright while still resembling natural tooth colour, rather than an artificial, opaque white.

faq.q: Is B1 the whitest tooth shade?
faq.a: B1 is the lightest shade on the classic VITA scale, but it is not the whitest option available. Dedicated bleach shades are whiter still. Many patients choose B1 because it gives a noticeably bright smile without looking unnatural next to the face, lips and skin tone.

faq.q: What is the difference between A1 and B1 tooth shades?
faq.a: A1 and B1 are both light shades, but they belong to different colour groups. A1 sits in the A group, which has slightly reddish-brown hues, while B1 sits in the B group, with reddish-yellow hues. In practice, B1 tends to look a touch brighter and cleaner, and A1 slightly warmer.

faq.q: How do I choose the right tooth shade for veneers or crowns?
faq.a: Choose your shade by considering your skin tone, the colour of your remaining natural teeth, your age, the lighting you are usually seen in and your personal style. The material also matters, because porcelain and zirconia reflect light differently. Your dentist will check the shade under different light before treatment.

faq.q: Will B1 match my natural teeth?
faq.a: B1 will only match your natural teeth if they are already very light. If you are treating just a few teeth, the new restorations need to blend with the teeth around them, so a darker shade may look more natural. For a full smile makeover, you have more freedom to choose B1.

title: Bad Breath After Tooth Extraction: Causes & Aftercare Tips
description: Bad breath after a tooth extraction is common and usually temporary. Learn the causes, from blood clots to dry socket, and when to contact your dentist.
h1: Bad Breath After Tooth Extraction: Causes and Care Tips

h2_changes.new: What is normal after a tooth extraction?
Why do you get bad breath after a tooth extraction?
Bad breath after tooth extraction: FAQs

faq.q: Is bad breath normal after a tooth extraction?
faq.a: Yes, bad breath after a tooth extraction is common and usually temporary. It is generally part of the normal healing process and not a cause for immediate concern. It should improve as the socket heals, provided you keep your mouth clean and follow your dentist’s aftercare instructions.

faq.q: What causes bad breath after a tooth extraction?
faq.a: The main causes are blood collecting around the socket, bacteria growing in the blood clot, infection of the wound, dry socket and reduced oral hygiene because brushing near the site feels uncomfortable. Bacteria that thrive without oxygen break down blood and debris, producing an unpleasant smell and taste, often worse at night.

faq.q: How can I tell if bad breath means I have dry socket?
faq.a: Dry socket is likely if pain returns or persists after the initial post-operative pain has eased, together with a bad taste and smell. It happens when the blood clot fails to form or dislodges, leaving bone exposed. It is more common in the lower jaw, in smokers and in women taking the contraceptive pill.

faq.q: When should I see a dentist about bad breath after an extraction?
faq.a: See your dentist straight away if bad breath comes with fever, pus or severe pain, as these can be signs of infection. You should also contact the clinic if pain does not respond to painkillers, which may point to dry socket. Untreated infections can lead to more serious health problems.

faq.q: Can I use a straw after a tooth extraction?
faq.a: No, you should avoid using a straw after a tooth extraction. The suction can pull the blood clot out of the socket, causing bleeding and increasing the risk of dry socket. Also keep your tongue, toothbrush and hard foods away from the clot while it heals.

title: Can You Have Dental Implants with Gum Disease? Antalya Guide
description: Yes, you can have dental implants with gum disease once it has been treated. Learn why healthy gums matter and contact us for a treatment plan.
h1: Can You Have Dental Implants with Gum Disease?

h2_changes.new: Dental implants and gum disease: FAQs

faq.q: Can you get dental implants if you have gum disease?
faq.a: Yes, you can have dental implants if you have gum disease, but the gum disease must be properly treated first. Healthy gums are one of the basic criteria for implant treatment, alongside sufficient bone density and volume. At Akdeniz Dental in Antalya, any gum treatment needed is planned before implant surgery.

faq.q: Why must gum disease be treated before dental implants?
faq.a: Gum disease must be treated first because it is an infection of the tissues that hold teeth and implants in place. Healthy gums protect the jawbone from bacteria and food debris. If periodontal disease is left untreated, it can lead to bone and tooth loss, which also threatens the stability of an implant.

faq.q: What is the difference between gingivitis and periodontitis?
faq.a: Gingivitis is the first, reversible stage of gum disease, with red, swollen gums that bleed when brushing but no bone loss. Periodontitis is the advanced stage, where gums recede, pockets form and bacteria reach the bone and roots, leading to heavy bleeding, gaps between teeth and loose teeth.

faq.q: How long does it take for a dental implant to heal?
faq.a: After an implant is placed, there is usually a waiting period of about three months while it fuses with the bone and surrounding tissues. During this time you are usually fitted with a lightweight temporary fixed prosthesis. Once healing is complete, the permanent fixed prosthesis is attached to the implant.

faq.q: Will I feel pain during dental implant surgery?
faq.a: You should not feel pain during the procedure itself, because a local anaesthetic is applied before the implant is placed. Dental implant treatment is still a surgical procedure, so follow your dentist’s aftercare advice during healing and ask the clinic if you have any concerns afterwards.

title: Dental Implant Removal: When and How Are Implants Removed?
description: Can dental implants be removed? Learn when implant removal is needed, how it is done under local anaesthesia and when a new implant can be placed again.
h1: Can Dental Implants Be Removed? Dental Implant Removal Guide

h2_changes.old: When is it necessary to remove the implant? 4 Cases
h2_changes.new: When does a dental implant need to be removed? 4 cases
How is a dental implant removed?

h2_changes.old: Can a new dental implant be placed?
h2_changes.new: Can a new implant be placed after removal?
Dental implant removal: FAQs

faq.q: Can dental implants be removed?
faq.a: Yes, dental implants can be removed. The procedure can be fairly invasive, and depending on the condition of the bone around the implant, additional surgical procedures may be required. The health of the bone and surrounding tissues is assessed before removal so the site can heal well afterwards.

faq.q: Why would a dental implant need to be removed?
faq.a: The four main reasons are trauma to the jawbone, infection such as peri-implantitis, a loose implant caused by poor healing or low bone density, and, rarely, an allergic reaction to titanium. Peri-implantitis is one of the most common reasons, as inflammation gradually causes bone loss around the implant.

faq.q: How is a dental implant removed?
faq.a: Implant removal is a surgical procedure usually carried out under local anaesthesia, starting with a small incision. A loose implant can often be removed with an implant torque wrench, while a firmly fixed one may need bone forceps, a specialised Lindemann bur or, more recently, laser techniques to protect the surrounding tissues.

faq.q: Can a new implant be placed straight after removal?
faq.a: Sometimes. If the bone defect is slight, a new implant can be placed immediately, although a larger diameter may be needed. With severe inflammation or bone loss, a healing period of a few days to several weeks is required first, so the infection is controlled and the bone can regenerate.

faq.q: How common is dental implant removal?
faq.a: Implant removal is uncommon. Just under three per cent of dental implants need to be replaced or removed within five years. Good oral hygiene and regular check-ups help prevent problems such as gum disease and peri-implantitis, which are among the main causes of implant failure.

What are the pros of E-max veneers?

E-max veneers: frequently asked questions

faq.q: What are E-max veneers made of?
faq.a: E-max veneers are made of lithium disilicate, a type of glass ceramic containing lithium and silicate. They are metal-free, ultra-thin and custom-made for each tooth, which allows them to combine strength with a natural, translucent appearance on the front surface of the teeth.

faq.q: Are E-max veneers better than other types of veneers?
faq.a: E-max veneers are thinner and stronger than many alternatives, such as standard porcelain, composite and Lumineers, and they usually need less tooth reduction. Their risk of cracking and fracture is lower than other porcelain veneers. The best option still depends on your teeth, bite and goals, which your dentist assesses.

faq.q: Do E-max veneers stain?
faq.a: E-max veneers are highly resistant to stains and discolouration caused by coffee, tea and smoking. This helps them keep their colour over time. Good oral hygiene is still important, because the natural tooth and gum line around the veneer can still be affected by plaque.

faq.q: Are E-max veneers reversible?
faq.a: No, E-max veneers are not reversible. A small amount of enamel is removed before they are bonded, so if you later decide to have them removed, your teeth will need to be reshaped or covered again with new veneers or other restorations. Consider this carefully before treatment.

faq.q: Will my teeth be sensitive after E-max veneers?
faq.a: Some people feel temporary, mild sensitivity after E-max veneers are fitted, which usually goes away within a week or two. Gum irritation is rare and is normally linked to a veneer that is not placed or bonded well, in which case your dentist can make the necessary adjustments.

faq.q: Why do E-max veneers cost more?
faq.a: E-max veneers are generally more expensive than other types of veneers because of the material and the precision involved. The final cost depends on the number of veneers needed, any extra procedures such as tooth preparation or gum shaping, and the experience of the dentist. Ask Akdeniz Dental for a personal treatment plan.

title: How Long After Dental Implants Can I Eat Normally? | Diet
description: Most people return to a normal diet one to two weeks after dental implant surgery. See what to eat in the first 48 hours, foods to avoid and healing tips.
h1: How Long After Dental Implants Can I Eat Normally?

h2_changes.new: What can you eat after dental implant surgery?

h2_changes.old: So, how long after dental implants can you eat normally?
h2_changes.new: How long after dental implants can you eat normally?

faq.q: How long after dental implants can I eat normally?
faq.a: Most people can return to a normal diet one to two weeks after dental implant surgery, depending on how extensive the surgery was and how quickly they heal. The first two weeks are the most critical, as gum tissue and bone stabilise around the implants, so soft foods are best during this time.

faq.q: What can I eat in the first 48 hours after dental implant surgery?
faq.a: Stick to soft, nutritious foods that need little chewing, such as yoghurt, applesauce, pureed vegetables, cottage cheese and tofu. Eggs and soft fish are also good choices because their protein supports tissue healing. Avoid acidic or spicy foods such as lemonade and tomatoes, which can worsen swelling.

faq.q: What foods should I avoid after dental implants?
faq.a: Avoid hard foods such as nuts and raw vegetables, sticky foods like toffee and caramel, crunchy crisps and crackers, spicy dishes, tough meats such as steak, hard sweets, chewing gum and popcorn. These can put pressure on the implant site, leave debris or irritate healing tissue. Alcohol should also be avoided.

faq.q: Can I drink through a straw after dental implant surgery?
faq.a: No, avoid using a straw after dental implant surgery. Sucking through a straw creates a vacuum that can pull out the blood clot at the surgical site, leading to a painful condition known as dry socket and slower healing. Drink directly from a glass instead.

faq.q: Can I have hot or fizzy drinks after dental implants?
faq.a: It is best to avoid hot and fizzy drinks in the first days after dental implant surgery. They can increase blood flow to the area, prolonging bleeding and irritating the surgical site, and may make swelling worse. Plenty of cool or room-temperature water is a better choice while you heal.

title: How Long Do All-on-4 Dental Implants Last? Lifespan Guide
description: With good care, All-on-4 implants can last 20 years or more. Learn how smoking, diabetes, bridge material and check-ups affect lifespan. Contact us.
h1: How Long Do All-on-4 Dental Implants Last?

faq.q: How long do All-on-4 dental implants last?
faq.a: Under ideal conditions and with the right care, All-on-4 implants can last more than 20 years or even a lifetime. Their lifespan depends on oral hygiene, smoking, general health, bone quality, implant quality and the design and material of the bridge, as well as regular professional check-ups.

faq.q: Does smoking shorten the life of All-on-4 implants?
faq.a: Yes. Smoking reduces blood circulation around the implants by up to 70% and can lead to bone loss. Implant failure rates are reported to be three times higher in people smoking more than 10 cigarettes a day, and lifespan may fall to 5–10 years. Stop at least 2 weeks before surgery and avoid smoking for 3 months afterwards.

faq.q: How long does the All-on-4 bridge last?
faq.a: It depends on the material. Zirconium bridges withstand high chewing forces and keep their colour for around 15 years. Hybrid acrylic bridges with a metal substructure last about 10–12 years, while more economical PMMA acrylic bridges usually need renewing every 5–7 years.

faq.q: How often should All-on-4 implants be checked?
faq.a: All-on-4 implants should be checked every 3 months during the first year and every 6 months after that. A periapical X-ray once a year, or a CBCT scan every 3 years, helps monitor the bone. Professional cleaning twice a year greatly reduces the risk of peri-implantitis.

faq.q: Can I have All-on-4 if I have diabetes?
faq.a: Yes, if your diabetes is well controlled, the risk of implant loss is close to normal. Uncontrolled diabetes, however, increases the risk of implant loss around four-fold. Tell your dentist about your condition and medication so your All-on-4 treatment in Antalya can be planned safely.

title: Inlay vs Onlay vs Crown: Which Tooth Restoration Is Best?
description: Inlay, onlay or crown? Learn how each restoration differs, how much natural tooth it keeps and when dentists recommend it. Get a treatment plan in Antalya.
h1: Inlay, Onlay or Crown: Which Restoration Do You Need?

h2_changes.old: What are the differences between Inlays and Onlays vs. Crowns?
h2_changes.new: What is the difference between inlays, onlays and crowns?

h2_changes.old: Which treatment option is preferred and when?

h2_changes.old: Comparison of Inlay Onlay vs Crown
h2_changes.new: Inlay vs onlay vs crown: comparison

faq.q: What is the difference between an inlay, an onlay and a crown?
faq.a: The difference is how much of the tooth each one covers. An inlay fits within the cusps of a tooth, an onlay covers one or more cusps, and a crown covers the entire visible tooth. Inlays and onlays are more conservative, preserving more natural tooth structure than a crown.

faq.q: When is an inlay used instead of a filling?
faq.a: An inlay is used when a cavity or damage is too large for a regular filling but not severe enough to need a crown. It is a custom-made restoration crafted in a dental laboratory to fit the prepared cavity exactly, offering a durable and natural-looking result for medium to large cavities.

faq.q: When do I need an onlay rather than a crown?
faq.a: You may need an onlay when damage extends to one or more cusps and is too extensive for a filling, but enough healthy tooth remains that a full crown is not necessary. An onlay reshapes and protects the affected part of the tooth while keeping more of its natural structure.

faq.q: What are inlays and onlays made of?
faq.a: Inlays and onlays are usually made from composite, ceramic or similar durable materials. They are custom-made in a dental laboratory from precise measurements or an impression, and their shape and colour are matched to your natural teeth so the restoration blends in.

faq.q: Is an inlay better than an amalgam filling?
faq.a: Inlays are often preferred over amalgam (silver) fillings because they look more natural and preserve more of the natural tooth structure. Because they sit within the chewing surface and are bonded to the tooth, they can also help strengthen it. Your dentist will advise which option suits your tooth.

title: Kill Tooth Nerve Pain in 3 Seconds? Myths and Real Relief
description: Can you kill tooth nerve pain in 3 seconds permanently? No, but it can be eased. Learn the causes of nerve pain, safe relief and when to see a dentist.
h1: Can You Kill Tooth Pain Nerve in 3 Seconds Permanently?

h2_changes.old: What is dental nerve pain, and how do we understand dental nerve pain?
h2_changes.new: What is dental nerve pain and what does it feel like?

h2_changes.old: When should you see a doctor for dental nerve pain?
h2_changes.new: When should you see a dentist for tooth nerve pain?
Tooth nerve pain: frequently asked questions

faq.q: Can you kill tooth nerve pain in 3 seconds permanently?
faq.a: No, killing tooth nerve pain in 3 seconds permanently is an urban legend. Some methods can ease the pain temporarily, but lasting relief only comes from finding and treating the underlying cause, such as decay, infection or a cracked tooth. Early dental treatment often keeps the problem under control.

faq.q: What causes tooth nerve pain?
faq.a: Common causes include deep tooth decay, a tooth abscess or infection, pulpitis (inflammation of the pulp), gum recession exposing the root, teeth grinding, cracked or broken teeth and trauma. Sinus infections can also press on the roots of the upper teeth, and pain can follow fillings, root canal treatment, whitening or extractions.

faq.q: What does tooth nerve pain feel like?
faq.a: Tooth nerve pain is usually sharp and severe. It may come in waves lasting seconds to minutes, become constant or worse at night, and spread to the jaw, ear, head, neck or temple. It often increases when chewing or pressing on the tooth and with hot or cold food and drinks.

faq.q: When should I see a dentist for tooth nerve pain?
faq.a: See a dentist if tooth nerve pain becomes persistent or keeps getting worse, as professional treatment is needed at that point. Seek help promptly if you notice swelling, redness or heat around the tooth, which can be signs of infection. Treating the cause early is the key to permanent relief.

title: Veneers vs Crowns: Key Differences and Which to Choose
description: Veneers vs crowns: learn how they differ, which materials are used and when each is recommended for looks or protection. Get a treatment plan in Antalya.
h1: Veneers vs Crowns: What Is the Difference?

h2_changes.new: What are dental veneers?
What are dental crowns?

h2_changes.old: What are the differences between Veneers and Crown?
h2_changes.new: What is the difference between veneers and crowns?
Veneers vs crowns: FAQs

faq.q: What is the difference between a veneer and a crown?
faq.a: A veneer is a thin shell bonded to the front surface of a tooth, mainly to improve its appearance. A crown is a cap that covers the whole tooth to restore and protect it after damage. Veneers address aesthetic concerns, while crowns are chosen when the tooth itself needs strengthening.

faq.q: When is a crown better than a veneer?
faq.a: A crown is usually the better choice when a tooth is fractured, cracked, decayed or weakened, or after root canal treatment or a large filling. Crowns are also used to hold a dental bridge in place and to cover dental implants. Veneers suit teeth that are structurally sound but need cosmetic improvement.

faq.q: What are dental veneers made of?
faq.a: Dental veneers are made from porcelain, composite resin or ceramics. Popular options include porcelain and laminate veneers, zirconium veneers and E-max veneers made of lithium disilicate, which are very thin, translucent and durable. Composite veneers are applied in layers directly to the teeth and then shaped and polished.

faq.q: What are dental crowns made of?
faq.a: Crowns can be made of metal, porcelain fused to metal, all-ceramic porcelain, resin, zirconium or E-max. Metal crowns are usually used on back teeth for strength, while metal-free crowns such as zirconium and E-max suit people who want a natural look or are allergic to metal.

faq.q: How do I know whether I need a veneer or a crown?
faq.a: Your dentist decides after examining your teeth, using intraoral checks and dental scanning to identify the problem and its cause. They then consider your preferences and recommend the right option. At Akdeniz Dental in Antalya, this assessment is the first step of any treatment plan.

title: Screwless Dental Implants: Screw-Retained vs Bonded Implants
description: What are screwless dental implants? Learn how press-fit and bonded implants differ from screw-retained ones, plus the pros and cons of each.
h1: What Are Screwless Dental Implants? Screw vs Bonded Implants

h2_changes.new: What are screwless dental implants?

h2_changes.old: How to do a screwless implant?
h2_changes.new: How is a screwless implant placed?
Why are dental implants important?

h2_changes.old: Screw-Retained Implant and Bonding Implant Method
h2_changes.new: Screw-retained vs bonded implants: how do they work?

faq.q: What are screwless dental implants?
faq.a: Screwless dental implants, also called press-fit or friction-fit implants, are designed so that no screw is needed to hold the abutment. The components are manufactured to fit together very precisely, and adhesive may be used to strengthen the connection. The main benefits are no risk of screw loosening and no visible screw holes.

faq.q: Do screwless implants really have no screws?
faq.a: Not always. The term screwless can be misleading, because in many so-called screwless or bonded systems a screw is still used. The difference is that adhesive, rather than a screw, fixes the crown to the implant at the visible connection point, so no screw access hole can be seen from the outside.

faq.q: What is the difference between screw-retained and bonded implants?
faq.a: In screw-retained implants, the crown and abutment are held together with a screw, which allows predictable results and strong resistance to chewing forces but leaves an access hole. In bonded, or cement-retained, implants the crown is bonded instead, so there is no screw hole and the restoration looks more natural.

faq.q: Which type of implant is better for front teeth?
faq.a: Bonded (cement-retained) implants are generally better for front teeth, where appearance matters most, because they have no visible screw access hole. Screw-retained implants are less suited to front teeth for aesthetic reasons, but they are valued elsewhere for durability, stability and predictable osseointegration.

faq.q: What are the advantages of screw implants?
faq.a: Screw implants are durable and long-lasting, show good primary stability and osseointegration, and resist the loads of chewing well. Once they have integrated with the bone, they do not loosen, which helps limit bone loss. They are mainly made of titanium or titanium alloy, which is highly biocompatible.

title: Problems with All-on-4 Dental Implants: Risks Explained
description: What problems can occur with All-on-4 implants? Learn about implant failure, peri-implantitis, bridge issues and nerve risks, and how to reduce them.
h1: What Are the Problems with All-on-4 Dental Implants?

h2_changes.old: What are the problems with all-on-4 dental implants?
h2_changes.new: Common All-on-4 complications and how to minimise them

faq.q: What are the most common problems with All-on-4 implants?
faq.a: The main potential problems are implant failure due to poor osseointegration, infection and peri-implantitis, mechanical issues with the bridge, bone or gum problems, nerve damage and aesthetic or functional dissatisfaction. Problems are rare when All-on-4 is carried out by an experienced dentist with careful planning.

faq.q: Why do All-on-4 implants fail?
faq.a: All-on-4 implants usually fail when they do not integrate properly with the bone, which can cause loosening or loss of the implant. Common causes are insufficient bone density, poor oral hygiene and smoking. Detailed bone analysis with 3D imaging before treatment helps the surgeon plan implant placement precisely.

faq.q: Can All-on-4 cause nerve damage?
faq.a: Nerve damage is possible if implants are placed incorrectly, especially in the lower jaw, and can cause lasting pain. Advanced imaging such as CBCT shows exactly where the nerves are, so an experienced surgeon can place the implants at a safe distance and keep this risk low.

faq.q: What happens if my All-on-4 bridge cracks or loosens?
faq.a: Cracks, fractures or loose screws are mechanical problems that can affect fixed All-on-4 bridges, and they should be checked by your dentist. Using durable materials such as zirconium or high-quality acrylic, and close cooperation between the surgeon and dental technicians on fit and bite, reduces the risk.

faq.q: Will I need a bone graft for All-on-4?
faq.a: Not always. All-on-4 has an advantage for patients with limited bone volume, but additional bone grafting or a sinus lift may still be needed in some cases. This is decided during detailed pre-treatment planning, so you know before travelling whether extra procedures are required.

title: Will All on 4 Teeth Look Natural? Smile Design in Antalya
description: Yes, All on 4 implants can look natural. Learn how tooth shape, position, colour and artificial gum design create a natural smile in Antalya, Turkey.
h1: Will All on 4 Dental Implants Look Natural in Antalya?

faq.q: Will All on 4 teeth look natural?
faq.a: Yes, All on 4 teeth can look natural without being excessively white or too large for your face. The result depends on the design of the bridge: the size and shape of the visible teeth, their position, and any gum-coloured material around them. At Akdeniz Dental in Antalya, these are planned around your face.

faq.q: Will All on 4 teeth look bulky or fake?
faq.a: They should not, if the cause of any bulk is identified and planned for. Too big can mean long front teeth, excess width, forward projection or fullness beneath the lip. There is a practical limit to how thin a bridge can be, because it holds the implant connections and carries chewing forces.

faq.q: Why might my All on 4 bridge need artificial gum?
faq.a: After teeth are lost, the jawbone and gum ridge gradually shrink, leaving extra space under the teeth. A pink, gum-coloured section of the bridge fills part of that volume so the teeth keep natural proportions instead of being unusually long. It can also support the lip, but it does not regrow gum or bone.

faq.q: Will the pink gum section show when I smile?
faq.a: It can, especially if your upper lip lifts high when you smile. With a low smile line, the lip may hide where the bridge meets your natural tissue. Your dentist assesses your full smile, speech and laughter during planning, so visible artificial gum is shaped to look convincing.

faq.q: Can bright All on 4 teeth still look natural?
faq.a: Yes, you do not need a dark shade for a natural look. Bright teeth can still have depth and detail, as natural enamel reflects light and lets some pass through near the edges. A shade looks stronger across a full arch, so it is compared with your opposite jaw when only one jaw is treated.

faq.q: How can I help plan a natural All on 4 smile in Antalya?
faq.a: Bring old photographs that show what you liked about your teeth before they were lost or badly worn. Everyday pictures are useful, so you do not need perfect close-ups. They help the dental team understand the tooth shape, length and position you want from your All on 4 bridge.
